sex.evidence: adult Sprague Dawley rats, n = 42, 21 male, 21 female

dosing.evidence: Group 1 (n = 14, 6 male, 8 female) received an intravenous bolus of 1 mg/kg psilocybin, Group 2 (n = 12, 6 male, 6 female) received an intravenous bolus of 10 mg/kg psilocybin, and Group 3 (n = 13, 6 male, 7 female) received an intravenous bolus of 0.9% saline (vehicle control).

day_night_flipped.evidence: maintained on a 12h:12h light:dark cycle (lights on at 08:00); Nociceptive responses were obtained between 12:00 and 14:00

assays.assay_description: Mechanical sensitivity assessed using von Frey filaments of ascending thickness applied to the plantar surface of each hind paw; paw withdrawal threshold (g) measured. Rats placed in individual Plexiglas enclosures on a mesh stand and habituated 20–30 min prior. Tested across multiple days (Day -1 baseline, Day 0 post-formalin, Day 1 post-drug, then days 3, 5, 7, 14, 21, 28).

application_type.evidence: intravenous bolus of 1 mg/kg psilocybin ... 10 mg/kg psilocybin

setup_habituation.evidence: rats were allowed 20-30 minutes to habituate to von Frey testing apparatus before each experiment

setup_restrain.evidence: rats were placed in individual Plexiglas testing enclosures on a IITC von Frey mesh stand

food_restriction.evidence: Standard testing apparatus with no food in the chamber; ad libitum food in home cage

water_restriction.evidence: Standard testing apparatus with no water in the chamber; ad libitum water in home cage

time_to_assay.evidence: Approximately 3 h after psilocybin or vehicle infusion, we measured responses ... thereafter the responses were measured every other day during week 1, and then weekly for the next three weeks

sample_size.evidence: Group 1 (n = 14, 6 male, 8 female) ... Group 2 (n = 12, 6 male, 6 female) ... Group 3 (n = 13, 6 male, 7 female)

outcomes.summary: Both low (1 mg/kg) and high (10 mg/kg) doses of i.v. psilocybin significantly attenuated formalin-induced mechanical hypersensitivity in ipsilateral and contralateral hind paws on all testing days for up to 28 days post-administration. No sex differences observed.
outcomes.statistics: ipsilateral p < 0.01, contralateral p < 0.0001 (all testing days)
outcomes.evidence: the rats injected with psilocybin - low or high dose - showed a significant attenuation of formalin-induced mechanical hypersensitivity in both ipsilateral (p < 0.01, all testing days) and contralateral (p < 0.0001, all testing days) paws

B1_num_measures.evidence: withdrawal threshold in the hind paws ipsilateral as well as contralateral to the injection

B2_temporal_dynamics.evidence: single average threshold value per session; no within-session time-course analysis

B4_ethological.evidence: paw withdrawal is a reflexive nociceptive response, not an ethological behaviour

B5_social.evidence: rats placed in individual Plexiglas testing enclosures

B7_automated_classification.evidence: manual filament application with observer-scored withdrawal

B8_multivariate.evidence: univariate analysis with linear mixed model; no dimensionality reduction

assays.assay_description: Thermal sensitivity assessed on a metal hot plate set at 52.5 °C with a clear acrylic cylinder confining the rat; latency to paw withdrawal/lick (seconds) measured. Tested across multiple days (Day -1, Day 0, Day 1, then days 3, 5, 7, 14, 21, 28).

application_type.evidence: intravenous bolus of 1 mg/kg psilocybin ... 10 mg/kg psilocybin

setup_habituation.evidence: habituation explicitly described for von Frey only

setup_restrain.evidence: clear acrylic cylinder placed atop to confine the rats in a specified observation field

food_restriction.evidence: Standard testing apparatus with no food in the chamber; ad libitum food in home cage

water_restriction.evidence: Standard testing apparatus with no water in the chamber; ad libitum water in home cage

time_to_assay.evidence: Approximately 3 h after psilocybin or vehicle infusion, we measured responses ... thereafter the responses were measured every other day during week 1, and then weekly for the next three weeks

sample_size.evidence: Group 1 (n = 14, 6 male, 8 female) ... Group 2 (n = 12, 6 male, 6 female) ... Group 3 (n = 13, 6 male, 7 female)

outcomes.summary: Psilocybin showed limited efficacy on formalin-induced thermal hyperalgesia. High dose (10 mg/kg) significantly attenuated hyperalgesia only on the day of administration and day 5; low dose (1 mg/kg) attenuated it only on days 3, 5, and 21 post-injection.
outcomes.statistics: high dose: p = 0.008 (day of administration), p = 0.02 (day 5); low dose: p = 0.04 (day 3), p = 0.01 (day 5), p = 0.01 (day 21)
outcomes.evidence: the rats treated with high-dose psilocybin showed a significant attenuation of formalin-induced thermal hyperalgesia only on the day of psilocybin administration (p = 0.008) and on day 5 after psilocybin injection (p = 0.02) ... Low-dose psilocybin attenuated formalin-induced thermal hyperalgesia only on day 3 (p = 0.04), day 5 (p = 0.01), and day 21 (p = 0.01) post-psilocybin injection

B1_num_measures.evidence: thermal hyperalgesia was expressed as paw withdrawal latency (seconds)

judge_notes: Two distinct behavioural assays identified: von Frey (mechanical) and hot plate (thermal). All three candidates agreed on this split.

B1 for von Frey set to 1 (2-3 measures) because ipsilateral and contralateral paw thresholds are reported as separate measures (gptoss interpretation supported by the text); hot plate reports a single latency measure so B1=0.
D1 scored as 'Multiple discrete sessions' (score 1) — repeated test sessions across days, not continuous monitoring.
time_to_assay set to 'multiple' since recordings occurred at 3 h, day 3, 5, 7, 14, 21, 28 post-dose, with value_minutes=180 reflecting the first timepoint.
food/water_restriction set to 'during' per the rubric's guidance that standard short tests without food/water in the apparatus = 'during'.

Outcome direction scored as 'increase' since psilocybin increased paw withdrawal threshold/latency (i.e., decreased the hypersensitivity/hyperalgesia measure). Note candidates split between 'decrease' (attenuation of hypersensitivity) and 'increase' (raw threshold); using increase consistent with the directly measured variable.
